doc.title: SEW web — FITS spectrum / cube viewer & fitter
hdr.path.ph: FITS path on the server, or click Browse / Upload
hdr.path.ph.wasm: Workspace path (or drag & drop / upload a FITS file)
data.obsVac.title: Whether the FITS wavelength axis is air or vacuum; aligned with the template frame automatically when fitting
view.coadd.bin.title: Checked = PowerBin bin stack; unchecked = aperture stack
view.binsn.title: Target S/N for PowerBin (sqrt of (ΣF)²/ΣV; S/N estimated over 5300–5700 Å)
view.ap.unit.title: Aperture unit: pix = pixels; arcsec = converted with the WCS pixel scale
view.showbins: Draw bin edges / selected bin on image
view.hint: Click the image to pick a pixel; scroll to zoom the spectrum; double-click to reset.
lines.title: Spectral lines to annotate (line_use.dat, rest-frame vacuum wavelengths)
map.hint: Open a data cube to show the image
empty.p1: Open a file on the left to show the cube image / spectrum here.
empty.p2: Supports single-spectrum FITS (flux in HDU0 or any extension) and 3D cubes (spectral axis may be numpy axis 0/1/2, linear or log10).
fit.r.title: R = λ/Δλ
fit.fwhmc.title: constant FWHM [Å]
fit.dlam.title: pPXF needs a uniform log-wavelength grid: velscale = c·ln10·dlam. Default follows the template sampling
fit.dlam.in.title: log10 wavelength step per pixel (dex)
fit.dust.title: Attenuation 10^(-0.4·A_λ) applied to stellar templates; A_λ is fitted with other parameters (pPXF engine only)
dust.expr.title: A_λ (mag) expression; variables lam (Å), av, beta
dust.offnote: ⟹ ppxf-sew fits equivalent-width spectra; extinction is absorbed by att_curve, so no dust parameters are needed

fit.maskSync.title: Peak-window model arbitration mask of pPXF-SEW
splitter.title: Drag to resize the top/bottom areas (double-click to reset)
tip.refreshReset: Refreshing clears the current fit result
modal.title: Select a FITS file
modal.empty: No FITS files in this directory
modal.pickLocal: Choose a file on this computer…

status.manual: Set HDU/column manually then click Apply override

tpl.msg.dling: Downloading (large files may take a while)…
tpl.status.none: No templates available; download or upload an npz
dlam.hint.tplLog: ⟹ template dlam={dlam} dex/px, velscale ≈ {v} km/s (observed spectrum is already on a log grid, used as is)
dlam.hint.obsLog: ⟹ observed spectrum is already on a log grid (dlam={dlam} dex/px, velscale ≈ {v} km/s), used as is

dust.hint.none: ⟹ no extinction correction applied to stellar templates

dust.hint.custom: ⟹ custom A_λ(λ) expression (variables lam, av, beta), fitting A_V and β
r.noMasses: (this template library has no masses; mass-weighted values unavailable)
log.noerr: No error HDU provided; using residual noise estimate
log.wavesys: Observed λ: air → vacuum (fitting on a vacuum grid)
log.fewpix: Too few valid pixels; redshift fell back to 0
log.loggrid: Observed spectrum is already on a log grid → no resampling; only templates are resampled to the same Δlnλ grid
log.sewignore: ppxf-sew fits equivalent-width spectra (extinction absorbed by att_curve); dust settings ignored
ws.title: Workspace
ws.hint: Templates and fit results are stored in this browser (IndexedDB); nothing is uploaded.
ws.url.ph: http(s) URL of a template npz (CORS allowed)
ws.cacheDone: Cached {n} runtime files into the workspace
ws.permDenied: The browser does not allow writing to this workspace folder (the permission may have expired). Choose the folder again via "Choose folder…" and allow write access, or use "Private browser folder" (OPFS); alternatively open the page served by run.py on the server and save there.
wiz.title: Set up a workspace
wiz.desc: Pick a local folder to store templates, FITS files and fit results; the runtime is cached there so you don't download it again.
wiz.li3: data/ — imported FITS; cache/ — runtime copy
wiz.mirror: Save the runtime into the workspace (no re-download next time)
wiz.browserOnly: Using browser storage only; clearing site data removes everything.
wiz.unsupported: This browser cannot access folders; using browser storage only.
wiz.staticOnly: This page is served as a static site (no backend): compute and workspace run inside this browser, so only folders on this machine can be chosen. To use folders and compute on the SSH server, open the page served by run.py on that server (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8800).
ws.hint.srv: Templates and fit results are stored in this page's workspace: {root}
set.title: Workspace settings
set.workdirHint: Templates, FITS files and fit results are stored here. Type a path or use Browse…
set.staticHint: This page is a plain static deployment ({origin}) with no server backend, so “Choose folder” opens folders on this computer.
set.backLocalHint: Clears the server address and reloads; your previously authorised local folder is kept.
set.staticUseDep: To compute and read/write files on a server, use the “Connect a compute server” wizard below.
dep.title: Connect a compute server (deploy wizard)
dep.desc: This page is static and cannot open SSH by itself. Three steps: (1) server address; (2) deploy/workspace folders; (3) run the two generated commands, then click Check & connect. Afterwards the page talks to run.py over HTTP and both compute and files live on that server.
dep.s2: Workspace / deploy folder (code dir, workspace root)
dep.aHint: ① Run on the server (clone code and start run.py, loopback only):
dep.bHint: ② Run on your own computer (open the SSH tunnel):
dep.openHint: The address bar stays on this page (GitHub Pages); the server only provides the API. One click and compute, workspace and files all live on the server.
Once ② is running, click here: it opens http://127.0.0.1:port. Same UI as this page, but compute, workspace and files all live on the server — no bridge, no cross-origin.
dep.copiedA: Copied ① — paste it in the server terminal
dep.copiedB: Copied ② — paste it in your local terminal and keep it open
set.bridgeHint: Run tools/sew_bridge.py --ssh user@host on your own computer. It starts run.py on the remote side, opens an SSH tunnel and prints a local address (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8977). Put that address here and both compute and files live on that remote server.
set.bridgeFail: Cannot reach that address: the local bridge is not running, or the remote has no SEWweb
set.bridgeEmpty: Enter the bridge address first (printed when you run sew_bridge.py locally)
set.bridgeFail2: Cannot connect. Check: (1) run.py is running on the server; (2) an SSH tunnel exists on this machine (ssh -N -L 8899:127.0.0.1:8899 user@host) or the local bridge is running; (3) the server was started with --cors including this page's origin.
ws.firstHint: Tip: you can use the app without a workspace (data is kept in browser storage). Click SEWWweb at the top left to pick a folder.
ws.needDirHint: No server workspace yet: click SEWWweb at the top left and choose a folder under Workspace.
ws.unsetHint: Workspace is not set yet. Click the SEWweb logo to choose a folder.
